name: Zadok
overview: Zadok was a male priest from the tribe of Levi, serving during the reign of King David. He was the son of Ahitub and is noted for being a mighty man of valor. Zadok is part of the Aaronic priesthood through Eleazar, highlighting his important priestly lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Zadok means 'righteous one' in Hebrew, reflecting his character or role as a faithful priest. This proper name is attested in 2 Samuel 8:17.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Zadok as the son of Ahitub. It is inferred that Zadok was the father of Ahimaaz and an ancestor of Azariah, linking him to a priestly lineage recorded in later texts.
scriptureSignificance: Zadok's significance lies in his role as a faithful Aaronic priest during King David's reign, serving in a time of national consolidation and worship establishment. His designation as a mighty man of valor underscores his strength and dedication, both spiritually and possibly militarily. Through his priestly service, Zadok contributed to maintaining the worship and religious order established by God through Aaron's descendants.
